audit_findings.title: Consolidated owner earnings may not match the parent-common share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated owner earnings may include cash attributable to noncontrolling interests while per-share value uses only Pangaea common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The non-controlling ownership interest attributable to NBHC and its wholly-owned ship-owning subsidiaries amounts to approximately $ 44,423 and $ 45,608 as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated worksheet error, but the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially overstating value. Pangaea consolidates six vessels owned through a 67%-owned entity and a barge held through a 50%-owned entity. Filed noncontrolling equity was $46.053 million at June 30, 2026, equal to 15.2% of the $302 million base equity value, although book NCI is not itself the required valuation adjustment. FY2025 income attributable to NCI was $0.798 million, or 5.7% of the $14.0 million anchor, but that amount does not establish NCI's share of D&A, drydocking, working capital or terminal owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation by legal entity and ownership percentage, attribute every income, noncash, working-capital and capital-expenditure component to Pangaea common shareholders, and rerun all scenarios only if the $14.0 million anchor is not already parent-attributable.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat ring-fenced subsidiary cash as distributable parent cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.843 million identifiable third-party cash share; broader surplus-cash adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds consolidated cash at 100% even though portions may belong to noncontrolling owners or be unavailable because of entity, lender, covenant or operating-liquidity requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: The assets of consolidated VIEs can generally only be used to settle obligations of those respective entities and are not available to satisfy the obligations of the Company or other consolidated subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: A limited error is demonstrated: one-third of NBHC's $5.045 million and one-half of the deck-barge entity's $0.323 million of June 2026 cash total $1.843 million, or approximately $0.028 per Pangaea share, before considering any contractual allocation. The potentially larger issue remains unresolved. The $105.675 million cash addition equals 35.0% of base equity value, consolidated minimum liquidity is $18 million, and VIE assets generally cannot satisfy obligations outside their respective entities. The record does not identify how much of the remaining balance is genuine surplus cash, so the full correction is unquantified but reasonably capable of materially changing the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 cash schedule by legal entity, ownership, bank account and covenant; identify restricted, lender-controlled, noncontrolling, voyage-working-capital and minimum-liquidity amounts; then rerun the bridge using only parent-attributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual owner earnings may omit normalized vessel-replacement capital
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted replacement-capital allowance would reduce sustainable owner earnings and the terminal value supported by the continuing fleet.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company does not currently maintain reserves for vessel replacements and intends to finance future vessel acquisitions through internally generated cash flows, borrowings under its credit facilities, or additional equity or debt offerings.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved methodological possibility, not a demonstrated omission from the anchor worksheet. It is nevertheless material because the valuation assumes perpetual operations, approximately 49.7% of base value and 50.9% of bull value comes from terminal value, and the vessels have only about 5 to 20 years of remaining estimated lives. The company maintains no replacement reserve and expects future acquisitions to be funded with cash flow, debt or equity. The filed $18.7 million estimate for 2026 special and intermediate surveys demonstrates capital intensity but does not quantify vessel-replacement capital because surveys and replacement are different requirements.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $14.0 million anchor to drydocking, ordinary maintenance, improvements and vessel purchases; develop a cycle-normalized annual replacement allowance from fleet ages, expected retirement dates, replacement costs and residual proceeds; rerun the scenarios if that allowance is absent.

audit_findings.title: The operating perimeter may double-count the Bulk Xaymaca sale
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 owner earnings may capitalize earnings from a vessel sold before the valuation date while the June 2026 cash bridge may also include its sale proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 27, 2026, the Company entered into a memorandum of agreement to sell the M/V Bulk Xaymaca for $ 9.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: Bulk Xaymaca operated during FY2025, was sold on May 18, 2026 for $9.6 million, and the valuation uses FY2025 owner earnings with a June 2026 cash bridge and no perimeter adjustment. The sale produced approximately $9.678 million of reported vessel-and-equipment proceeds, equal to 3.2% of base equity value or about $0.15 per share, but those proceeds are not automatically an error. The actual double count depends on Bulk Xaymaca's contribution to the $14.0 million anchor and whether the proceeds remained in bridge cash; neither is supplied, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Calculate Bulk Xaymaca's FY2025 parent-attributable owner earnings and trace the $9.6 million proceeds through June 30 cash and debt. Rerun using a consistent perimeter—normally removing the sold vessel's recurring earnings while retaining only qualifying net sale cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain a temporary working-capital release
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.2 million, equal to 44.3% of the $14.0 million anchor; up to $87.2 million or $1.31 per share of base-value sensitivity if fully removed
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary working-capital inflow included in owner earnings would inflate the anchor and therefore forecast-period and terminal owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in operating assets and liabilities provided $6.2 million of cash in 2025 compared to $1.6 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $6.2 million FY2025 working-capital inflow is filed, but its inclusion without normalization is not demonstrated because the anchor worksheet is absent. If the full amount is embedded and nonrecurring, it represents 44.3% of the anchor. Because the DCF operating value scales with the anchor, full removal would reduce the stated $197 million base operating value by approximately $87.2 million, or $1.31 per share, before any bridge change. The sustainable correction could be smaller because individual receivable, inventory, payable and deferred-revenue movements may reflect normal growth requirements.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $14.0 million anchor to the cash-flow statement by working-capital account, separate sustainable operating needs from timing releases, and rerun every scenario with the normalized working-capital requirement.

audit_findings.title: A vessel-disposal gain may remain in recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.0 million, equal to 21.4% of the $14.0 million anchor; up to $42.2 million or $0.63 per share of base-value sensitivity if capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring disposal gain left in the anchor would be projected and capitalized as recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded a gain of $3.0 million related to the sale of two vessels.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated error: the filed cash-flow statement reverses the entire $3.0 million gain when reconciling net income to operating cash flow, which would remove it if the anchor was derived consistently from operating cash flow. The supplied record does not include the anchor worksheet, so inclusion remains unresolved. If the gain was retained, it equals 21.4% of the anchor and would increase base operating value by approximately $42.2 million, or $0.63 per share, making the possibility material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.0 million gain through the FY2025 owner-earnings worksheet. Close the finding if the operating-cash-flow reversal is preserved; otherwise remove the gain and rerun all scenarios without changing unrelated inputs.
